questions: When replacing every occurrence of x with y, does this also affect characters that were originally y (i.e., could it cause merging or collisions)?
Is the operation reversible or can we choose x and y arbitrarily each time, even if y is already present in S?
Do we consider the operation as atomic per step, meaning we cannot have intermediate states where both x and y are being changed simultaneously in one operation?
Are we allowed to choose x and y such that x equals y (a no-op)?
If S and T are already identical, is the minimum number of operations 0?
Does 'replace every occurrence of x in S with y' apply to the current S after previous operations, or only to the original S?
Can we choose x and y that are not necessarily distinct from characters in T, or are there restrictions based on T's letters?
Is the goal to make S identical to T exactly, or is it sufficient that after operations S equals T at that moment (even if further operations could change it)?
